evidence: the-peer-plays-the-relayhost: manifests/postfix_smtp_node.pp:17-18 look up the node's relayuser/relaypass (and 6-7 the relayport); the peer's stand-in creates exactly that account (p8test-relay with the lab Hiera fixture's password 'p8test-not-a-secret', master_fixtures.sh:134-135) and serves submission on 587 with relaying only for SASL-authenticated clients, so the node can only get a message through with the credentials those lines render; the effect (587 listening, dovecot active) is the setup's result, and the declared mutation matches the action line by line

effective-relay-config: main.cf:11-12 render myhostname=@hostname and myorigin=@myorigin; under the defaults fixture (lab Hiera myorigin mycompany.com) postconf -h expects puppet8node and mycompany.com, and the rest of the expected values follow the template lines 34-54 and the lookup defaults (mydestination=hostname, mynetworks 127.0.0.0/8, 10240000) and the Debian CA path of manifest lines 29-32; ok
postfix-running-and-enabled: manifest lines 68-72 declare service postfix ensure running, enable true; systemctl is-active/is-enabled expecting active/enabled tests exactly that; ok

purpose covered: Purpose (header line 2: send mail from a non-specialised node by means of a relayhost) is stated right and tested as behaviour: a message submitted on the node leaves the queue with status=sent to mailserver.mycompany.com:587 (name pinned to the peer, fence on mail ports to any other address), arrives in the peer's mailbox received 'with ESMTPSA' (STARTTLS + SASL) and the peer logs sasl_username=p8test-relay, which can only succeed with the class's sasl_passwd credentials since the stand-in rejects unauthenticated relay; a 10.5 MB submission is refused by postfix's sendmail ('too big', non-zero exit; the refusal is synchronous, so the tool's exit status and diagnostic are the result itself); the peer (outside mynetworks) gets 454 Relay access denied on port 25 (main.cf:31,35); configuration, postfix check, compiled SASL map (with a valid mismatch on the looked-up host), service state and the root alias rendering/compilation are probed. Honestly uncovered: the RedHat branch (cyrus-sasl-plain, ca-bundle.crt; rhel9) and non-default per-node Hiera values (one fixture per set). Notes, not gaps: message_size_limit's lookup default equals postfix's built-in default, so the size check cannot tell the class's value from postfix's; the open-relay check has no mismatch (e.g. a local recipient) though 'Relay access denied' is specific to the unauth-destination restriction.
